note: Promotion to the tracked schema (v0.91.0, prompt 3 tranche two). Each theme in this pack names exactly one row at one grade band, not five rows across the ladder, so "unbanded": true fills each row's empty description with its own complete sentence directly — no per-band suffix, since the row already names its own grade. track/code are not filled by this promotion (see tools/normalize_blocks.py apply_promotions): this pack's natural sub-groupings do not form the 50-block tracked shape. Theme text and grouping are copied verbatim from data/blocks.csv; nothing else is touched.

themes.description: Name the decider behind three real school rules and how you found out.
Ask for the reason behind a class rule and report the answer received.
Run a turn-taking system for an activity so nobody gets skipped.
Disagree with a classmate's idea in a role-play without naming or blaming them.
Name three people whose work a school depends on and thank one in person.
Make and keep a week-long class commitment, recorded publicly.

themes.theme: How a class decision is made (CF)
themes.description: Chair a five-minute class decision and produce the written record.
Take minutes of a real meeting and have two attendees confirm them.
Run a vote and then state what will be done for those who lost it.
Map an address to its ward, district and board seat and name the office holder.
Trace something in a classroom back to the budget line that paid for it.
Send a real request to a real office and log what comes back.

themes.theme: Reading a sign, reading a rule (CF)
themes.description: Find a posted public rule, explain it plainly, and identify who set it.

themes.theme: Fair is a word people argue about (CF)
themes.description: Argue both sides of a fairness case and say which side you would choose and why.
Diagram a parish's three governing functions and name a real holder of each.
Identify the decisive meeting for a local issue and prove it from the record.

themes.theme: Public records, and how to ask (CF)
themes.description: File a real records request and document the response or the silence.
Locate a real budget line, explain it, and state what a ten percent change would do.
Deliver two minutes of testimony to a panel and pass the observer's rubric.

themes.theme: Who is not in the room (CF)
themes.description: Audit a real decision for who was absent and propose how they would be reached.
Mediate a scripted dispute to a written agreement both sides sign.
Write a letter that receives a substantive reply, and file both.
Trace an ordinance from proposal to adoption and name every gate it passed.
Map a real school decision to the exact body with authority over it.
Compare two years of a real budget and write what changed in priority terms.
Build a civic argument on public data and state its three biggest weaknesses.
Chair a public meeting with a real agenda and produce approved minutes.
Complete a real conflict-of-interest disclosure for a project and have it reviewed.
Give an on-record interview in a simulation and produce an accurate account of it.
Take a refused request, diagnose why, and produce a revised route to yes.
Draft a real local ordinance and have it reviewed by a practicing attorney.
Produce a fiscal note for a proposal that a finance officer accepts.
Assemble a coalition of three parties with a written statement all three sign.
Hand over a documented civic project that a successor can run unaided.
Recruit and train a named successor who runs one session without you.
Present a complete public case to a panel that includes a dissenting member.
Publish an honest outcome report on a real project, including its failures.
Name four public workers you have met and say what each one does.
Visit a public building and report one thing anyone may use there.
Explain to a younger child why a queue exists and how to ask for help in one.
Give three examples of things everyone in a town may use.
Complete an emergency call script correctly under observation.

themes.theme: Thank the work, not the person (PS)
themes.description: Interview a public worker about their hours and report what was learned.
Explain a real department to a peer using only what has been verified.
Complete a real public form correctly and describe where it goes next.
Observe a real service point for thirty minutes and report three friction points.
Rewrite a real public notice in plain language and test it on a family.
Map the true travel cost of a service for one neighbourhood.
Find an unnecessarily identifying step in a real service and propose its removal.
File a real, fair complaint and track what it changed.
Conduct and write up an interview the subject agrees is accurate.

themes.theme: How a public job is filled (PS)
themes.description: Map a real public job from posting to first day, with dates and requirements.
Trace a real purchase through its approval steps and name each safeguard.
Measure a real service's response time and present it without assigning blame.
Explain a parish's plan for one hazard and find a gap in it.
Map a real school-to-health-department route from end to end.
Trace a utility from its source to a tap or bin and name every operator involved.
Resolve three scripted counter dilemmas and defend each decision made.
Run a volunteer shift that the host confirms reduced their workload.
Diagram an agency from its mandate to its front line and name the failure point.
Write a real grant application and submit it with a named sponsor.
Complete a supervised case file to resolution or a documented handover.
Design a service data plan that a privacy officer approves.
Audit a real service for access and produce a costed remediation list.
Run a tabletop exercise in a named role and produce the log of it.
Read a real contract and write the three questions its overseer should ask.
Analyse a real vacancy pattern and propose two retention measures.
Design a service and pass review by a panel that includes a serving administrator.
Produce a defensible cost-per-outcome figure for a real program.
Shadow or reconstruct an inspection and write what it did and did not fix.
Broker a written agreement between two real organisations.
Deliver a crisis briefing under questioning and pass the observer's rubric.
Publish an evaluation that reports at least one negative finding honestly.
Produce a costed five-year plan into a named public role and defend it.
Get two classmates to join a small ask and report what happened.
Turn a class complaint into one sentence and get five people to say it back.
Interview three classmates about a problem and report their words, not your own.
Invite five people to something and accept every no without argument.
Run a three-person commitment for a week and report the drop-outs honestly.
Retell an event accurately after hearing an exaggerated version of it.
Write an ask that names the person, the action and the deadline.
Map ten people affected by an issue and rank them by their stake in it.

themes.theme: The meeting people come back to (CB)
themes.description: Run three meetings where attendance does not fall.
Assign four roles for a project and have each one fulfilled by its owner.
Produce a poster that a stranger can act on without asking a question.
Report a real supporter count with each category kept separate.
Hold a five-minute disagreement that both sides describe as respectful.
Close an unsuccessful effort with a written account its members endorse.
Produce a power map for a real issue and defend every arrow drawn on it.
Write a campaign plan with a named stop condition and follow it through.
Predict attendance within twenty percent for a real event and report the miss.
Deliver a three-minute public narrative that an observer verifies as accurate.
Place an accurate story and document what was declined to be said.
Run a consented list and report the gap between followers and turnout.
Serve as a trained marshal in a supervised action with no incident.
Take a scripted offer to a group decision with the trade-offs written down.
Produce an issue brief that survives review by someone on the other side.
Obtain a real permit and brief participants on their rights and limits.
Draft an agreement that three organisations sign before any action.
Run a transparent fundraise and publish a full account of it.
Secure a meeting, brief a staffer, and report the outcome accurately.
Write the opposing brief and have an opponent confirm it is fair.
Run a rota with documented rest and no volunteer working two weeks straight.
Publish a campaign evaluation that separates outputs from outcomes.
Chair a live coalition through a contested decision to a signed outcome.
Convert a demand into a proposal a public official calls implementable.
Hand over a live effort that continues for a month without you.
Track a won commitment for a term and publish whether it was kept.
Publish a correction of your own campaign's claim and keep the coalition intact.
Train three successors who each lead one component unaided.
Present a full leadership portfolio to a panel that includes a community elder.
